[[File:Mike Thewalt 2017.jpg|thumb|Mike Thewalt in 2017]]

'''Michael L. W. Thewalt''' (born 5 December 1949 in [[Karlsruhe]], Germany)<ref name="AMWS">{{cite encyclopedia |editor=Henderson, Andrea Kovacs |encyclopedia=American Men & Women of Science |volume=7 T–Z |year=2010 |title=Thewalt, Michael L W |publisher=Gale |location=Detroit, Michigan |isbn=978-1-4144-4558-8 |page=1078 |edition=28th}}</ref> is a Canadian physicist. He received his BSc from [[McMaster University]] in 1972. His MSc and PhD were from the [[University of British Columbia]] in the mid-1970s. He teaches at [[Simon Fraser University]] and is known for researching [[semiconductor]]s,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rsc.sfu.ca/people/mthewalt.htm |work=RSC at SFU |title=Michael Thewalt |publisher=Simon Fraser University |accessdate=18 March 2013}}</ref> especially isotopically enriched silicon.

== Awards ==
*1994 [[Rutherford Memorial Medal]]
*2004 Brockhouse Medal<ref>[http://www.cap.ca/awards/press/2004-Thewalt-b.html Canadian Association of Physicists] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110527021900/http://www.cap.ca/awards/press/2004-Thewalt-b.html |date=2011-05-27 }}</ref>
*2013 SFU Dean's Award for Excellence in Graduate Supervision<ref>[https://www.sfu.ca/dean-gradstudies/blog/year/2013/10/MikeThewalt.html Simon Fraser University Graduate Studies]</ref>
